consensus_summary: Sword primarily symbolizes the Word of God as a penetrating spiritual weapon (Eph 6:17; Heb 4:12; Rev mouth-sword texts), with common alternatives of divine judgment, civil/governmental authority, and gospel division.
book_summary: Sword is the Word of God wielded by the Spirit to discern and execute judgment; also war and the governing force that carries judgment out; proceeds from Christ’s mouth, takes peace from the earth, and guards the way.
consensus_core_identification: Word of God (spiritual weapon of truth/discernment)
book_core_identification: Word of God for discernment and judgment execution, plus war and governing force that carries judgment
boundary_disagreement: Book folds war, judgment-execution, and governing authority into the core identification itself; consensus keeps Word of God as the distinct primary and lists those as separate common alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores share the identical primary referent (Word of God) and the same key texts; the book simply elevates and unifies the already-common judgment/war/authority senses that consensus already recognizes, producing a broader but non-contradictory extension rather than a replacement of the central identification.
strongest_objection: Unifying polyvalent, context-specific senses (Word vs. war vs. civil sword) into one core entry may over-smooth distinctions that consensus carefully preserves.
